parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Section four. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty on page eight.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

I'd like to give you a brief overview of a research project I've been working on as part of a team of four. We wanted to get some data on what happens to students after they graduate, and also find out how useful they felt their degree course was to them. We focused on graduates from the course in business management since this is one of the most popular and long-established courses. We decided to use two different data gathering methods. We started off by emailing a brief questionnaire to all last year's graduates from that course, and then we selected a number of those who had replied, and with them, we carried out phone interviews. We'd originally intended to use face-to-face interviews but didn't feel that would be practical. And in fact, we found this method provided a combination of wide coverage and depth, which is what we wanted.

So what did we find? Well, I suppose our most surprising finding was just how many graduates had gone on to work towards an additional qualification rather than getting a job immediately. That was thirty-two percent, almost a third. Of the rest, a very small proportion were unemployed, just four percent, and all the rest were in employment. More than half of them were in the public sector with a sizable minority in the private sector and a small number in the not-for-profit sector. We were also interested in the attitudes of those who were employed towards their work. The majority said that their expectations had been fulfilled. They were generally satisfied in terms of their salary and also happy with their prospects for career development, with very few of them feeling that they were in a dead-end job with no prospects of promotion.

For the second main part of our research, we wanted to get some feedback from the graduates on how useful they felt their degree course had been to them. There were really three main skills which the graduates felt they'd gained from doing the course and identified as having been the most valuable to them. They highlighted the fact that they developed the ability to work as members of a team. Another skill which they cited as valuable was that of personal organization, things like meeting deadlines, time management, and so on. And finally, a lot of them said that what they learned about approaches to problem-solving had been very useful.

We also asked them about which elements of the course had been least valuable to them. To our surprise, the thing that was mentioned most often here was presentations. They hadn't enjoyed having to give these as part of their course, nor had they found it useful having to listen to those given by their fellow students. The reason given for this was that they felt they weren't trained how to do it properly. And the second thing that got very negative feedback was work on essay writing. Most people thought this was unnecessary and that it would have been better to work on report writing. And finally, some respondents said that they would have liked more guidance on the best way to go about looking for a job, that the course could have done more to help them.

analyses.content: 录音明确提到他们将研究重点放在了工商管理（Business Management）课程的毕业生上。
We focused on graduates from the course in Business Management, since this is one of the most popular and long-established courses.
你可能会听到后面的“popular and long-established courses”而走神，要注意题目问的是哪一门具体的学科（subject），直接抓取核心课程名称即可。

We started off by emailing a brief questionnaire to all last year's graduates from that course, and then we selected a number of those who had replied, and with them, we carried out phone interviews. We'd originally intended to use face-to-face interviews but didn't feel that would be practical.
你可能会听到后面说的“face-to-face interviews（面对面采访）”想填，但录音紧接着用“but”转折，觉得这“不现实（wouldn't be practical）”，所以最终采用的是电话采访。
录音中提到这两种数据收集方法，一个是发邮件问卷，紧接着就是进行电话采访（phone interviews）。

Well, I suppose our most surprising finding was just how many graduates had gone on to work towards an additional qualification rather than getting a job immediately. That was thirty-two percent, almost a third.
这道题答案出现在定位词32%（thirty-two percent）之前，你需要在听到“surprising finding”时就集中注意力抓取核心名词，而不是等听到数字了再去回想。
录音中提到有32%的毕业生没有马上找工作，而是去获取额外的学历/资格证书（qualification）。
More than half of them were in the public sector, with a sizable minority in the private sector and a small number in the not-for-profit sector.
你可能会听到后面的“private”或者“not-for-profit”，但题目对应的是“most of students”，只有“More than half（超过一半）”修饰的public才是正确答案。
录音中明确指出超过一半（对应题干most）的毕业生在公共（public）部门工作。

They were generally satisfied in terms of their salary and also happy with their prospects for career development, with very few of them feeling that they were in a dead-end job with no prospects of promotion.
你可能会听到紧跟着的“career development”，但题目横线前没有介词，且salary是最直接对应“satisfied in terms of”的答案，填写salary最稳妥。
录音中提到他们总体上对薪水（salary）满意，也就是对应题目的happy with。
录音中提到他们重点强调了自己培养了作为团队（team）一员去工作的能力。
They highlighted the fact that they developed the ability to work as members of a team.
你可能会听到“members”想填上去，但题目上已经有了“member”，这里需要填的是修饰词，也就是“团队（team）”。
录音提到他们觉得学到的解决问题（problem-solving）的方法非常有用。
这种做修饰语的必须加连字符，所以不能填problem solving，语法错误。另外，你可能会听到前面的“approaches”就填，但题目搭配的是“ability”，对应录音里“approaches to”后面的核心能力，即“解决问题”。
And finally, a lot of them said that what they learned about approaches to problem-solving had been very useful.

We also asked them about which elements of the course had been least valuable to them. To our surprise, the thing that was mentioned most often here was presentations. They hadn't enjoyed having to give these as part of their course, nor had they found it useful having to listen to those given by their fellow students. The reason given for this was that they felt they weren't trained how to do it properly.
你可能会错过答案，因为这里话题刚从“有用的技能”转到“最没价值的技能（least valuable / useless）”，要敏锐抓取转折和引出新话题的词，比如“To our surprise”。
录音中明确提到最常被提及的（没用的部分）是演讲（presentations），因为他们觉得没有受过相关训练。
And the second thing that got very negative feedback was work on essay writing. Most people thought this was unnecessary and that it would have been better to work on report writing.
你可能会听到紧接着的“report writing”而错填，但录音明确用虚拟语气说的是“如果做报告写作（report writing）会更好”，说明他们实际上觉得没用的是论文写作（essay writing）。
录音指出第二件收到负面反馈（对应useless）的事情是论文写作（essay writing），受访者觉得这没必要（unnecessary）。
And finally, some respondents said that they would have liked more guidance on the best way to go about looking for a job, that the course could have done more to help them.
你可能会听到“guidance”想填进去，但题目是“finding a ___”，直接对应录音中的同义替换“looking for a ___”，抓取“job”即可。
录音最后提到，受访者希望在寻找工作（looking for a job）的最好方法上得到更多指导。
